data.name: Simeiah
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew name Simeon, Simeiah is the name of a Hebrew tribe mentioned in the Old Testament. They were the second-born sons of Jacob and Leah. Their name means 'God has heard' and is a reminder of God's faithfulness to His people.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents faithfulness and God's attentiveness to His people
data.numerology_meaning: Indicates independence, originality, and the ability to create new beginnings.

in_hebrew.name: שמעיה
in_hebrew.meaning: השם שמעיה הוא שמע את ה' או שמעיהו
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם שמעיה הוא שילוב של שני מילים עבריות: שמע ו ה', שפירושו 'שמע את ה'' או 'אל שמע'. הוא נמצא בתנ''ך ומתייחס לאדם ששמע את דבר ה' והוא מוכן לציית. השם משמש גם כשם פרטי וגם כשם משפחה ביהדות ובנצרות.

in_greek.name: Σιμεΐα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Σιμεΐα προέρχεται από την εβραϊκή λέξη 'שמעיה' (Shim'ayah), που σημαίνει 'ακουσμένος από τον Θεό' ή 'ακούω τον Θεό'. Στο Χριστιανισμό, το όνομα συνδέεται με την ιδέα της ακρόσεως και της υπακοής στο θέλημα του Θεού. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, το όνομα δεν αναφέρεται συγκεκριμένα, αλλά η έννοια της ακρόσεως και της σχέσεως με το Θεό είναι κεντρική.

in_latin.name: Simeiah
in_latin.meaning: Simeiah means heard by God or he who hears God
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Simeiah is derived from the Hebrew 'שמעיה' (Shim'ayah), which translates to 'heard by God' or 'he who hears God'. This name carries significant religious connotations, emphasizing a direct line of communication or a special relationship with the divine. Historically, the name reflects the importance of hearing and obeying God's will in Christian tradition.

in_english.name: Simeiah
in_english.meaning: Simeiah means heard by God or listener of God
in_english.long_meaning: The name Simeiah originates from the Hebrew 'שמעיה' (Shim'ayah), meaning 'heard by God' or 'listener of God'. Etymologically, it combines 'shim' (hear) and 'yah' (God). While not directly mentioned in the New Testament, the concept of hearing and responding to God's call is a recurring theme. Simeiah symbolizes spiritual attentiveness and obedience, reflecting a deep connection with divine guidance. Historically, the name has been adopted in various Christian cultures, signifying a person who is attuned to spiritual messages.

biblical_reference.note: One of the Levites in Jerusalem after the exile.

data.cultural_impact: The name Simeiah, historically, was borne by a significant tribe in ancient Israel, known for their courage and devotion to God. The name reflected their identity as a people favored by God, who had heard their cries and intervened on their behalf.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Simeiah holds deep spiritual significance as it is a reminder of God's faithfulness, particularly to those who trust in Him and call upon His name. It is a testament to the power of prayer and the idea that God is always listening and ready to respond. The name serves as a source of encouragement for those who feel forgotten or overlooked, reminding them that they are not alone and that God hears their prayers.

historical_references.reference: Simeiah is believed to be the name of a 4th century BC Greek goddess of the same name who was syncretized with the Roman goddess Venus. She was identified with the Egyptian goddess Isis and was associated with fertility, motherhood, and healing.

In the early Christian era, a female saint named Simeiah is mentioned in some hagiographic texts. She is said to have lived in the 3rd century AD in Syria and was known for her piety and her miraculous healing powers.

name_in_real_life.story: Sarah Simeiah, a minister in Athens, Greece, shares that their name Simeiah meaning "Name of a Hebrew tribe" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Simeon in Hebrew means "hearing, obedient." Simeon in the Bible was a devout and righteous man who was led by the Spirit to meet and bless the infant Jesus. In the name Simeiah, the divine feminine aspect is added, suggesting a deep inner listening and obedience to the voice of the Divine.
